html:
The first prime minister of the independent Congo, in office for less than three months in 1960, and later murdered. He became a symbol of African independence and of foreign meddling in it.

A former postal clerk, he founded the Congolese National Movement in 1958, the first party to work across the Belgian Congo rather than for one region or people. On independence day, 30 June 1960, he gave a speech before King Baudouin that bluntly listed the humiliations of colonial rule.

Within days the army mutinied, and the mineral-rich province of Katanga broke away with Belgian support. Lumumba asked the United Nations for help, then turned to the Soviet Union, which alarmed the West in the Cold War. President Joseph Kasavubu dismissed him, and army chief Mobutu took power. Lumumba was arrested, flown to Katanga and shot on 17 January 1961, with Belgian officers present. His death is at the heart of the Congo Crisis. In 2022 Belgium returned a tooth, his only known remains, to his family.
sum: The first prime minister of the independent Congo, in office for less than three months in 1960, and later murdered. He became a symbol of African independence and of foreign meddling in it.
